clue.text: Compose the line, then one bar of course

indicators.note: to compose is to put together or arrange, so the following words are rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: Instructions to write a line of verse and then a single bar of music, as if setting a song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Compose' suggests writing music or poetry, but it signals that THE LINE THEN ONE is rearranged. The definition is a golf joke: the bar on a golf course.
explanation.definitionFit: Golfers jokingly call the clubhouse bar the extra hole played after the eighteenth, so it is the drinking spot of a course.

clue.text: Troubles facing stern son when French cop enters

indicators.note: the French policeman goes into the middle of the word for the stern of a boat

parts.note: aft means towards the stern of a ship
flic is French slang for a policeman
S is the abbreviation for son in family trees

explanation.surface: A son facing the back of a boat while a French policeman boards: a family's worries at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Troubles' is a verb here: the answer is what something does when it bothers you.
explanation.definitionFit: To afflict someone is to cause them suffering, the same as giving them trouble or distress.

clue.text: Vocal elements ignored when replacing the video with this?

definitions.text: Vocal elements ignored when replacing the video with this?

indicators.note: placing the remaining letters afresh in a different order, re-placing them
vowels are the voiced, vocal elements of speech, so dropping them leaves only the consonants of the phrase

explanation.surface: A question about whether this new format would replace the old video recorder, with sound left out.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the vowels E, I, E, O from THE VIDEO to leave T, H, V, D; 'replacing' rearranges them. The whole clue also describes the format that superseded video tape.
explanation.definitionFit: High-definition television superseded videocassette viewing as the home picture format, so it is what replaced the video.

clue.text: Initially wet on the ground in Gabon, granule around noon is tending to stay dry

indicators.note: initially means at the beginning, so only the opening letter of the next word is used

parts.note: French is spoken in Gabon, and a terre is French for on the ground

indicators.note: the word for a granule goes round the letter for midday

parts.note: a pellet is a small grain or granule

explanation.surface: Rain falling on the ground in an African country, with a grain somehow keeping dry at midday.
explanation.walkthrough: Gabon is a French-speaking country, which tells you to put 'on the ground' into French: A TERRE.
explanation.definitionFit: A water-repellent fabric resists moisture, so it is inclined to keep from getting wet.

clue.text: Kid around?

parts.note: a kid is a young goat, so behaving as one would is literally fooling about like that animal

explanation.definitionFit: To act the goat is a British idiom for clowning or behaving foolishly, which is what kidding around means.

clue.text: Issue to make gal mad?

indicators.note: to make something out of letters is to reassemble them into a new word

explanation.surface: A question about what publication might enrage a young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Issue' is an edition of a magazine. The surface works too: a men's magazine might well make a woman angry.
explanation.definitionFit: A lad mag is a British term for a men's lifestyle magazine, and each edition of a periodical is an issue.

clue.text: No Muslim elected Castro, for example

parts.note: a candidate who is elected is in
Fidel Castro was the Cuban leader

explanation.surface: A political note that Castro, voted into power, was no follower of Islam.
explanation.definitionFit: Infidel is a term once used by Muslims for a non-believer in their faith.

clue.text: Scene of book borrowing line to finish with facile note about Resistance

parts.note: to end in is to finish with something
glib means superficially easy or facile

indicators.note: the musical note goes round the letter standing for resistance

parts.note: ray is the second note of the tonic sol-fa scale
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: Advice for a writer to close a line on a shallow note concerning the French underground movement.
explanation.walkthrough: Ray, also spelt re, is the note after doh in sol-fa.
explanation.definitionFit: A lending library is a place where members borrow books and return them later.

clue.text: A priest's assistant, moving right to the front, bowed

indicators.note: moving says one letter of the assistant's title is shifted to another position
to the front says the shifted letter goes to the start of the word

parts.note: a curate is a cleric who assists a parish priest

explanation.surface: A junior cleric steps forward to the front of the church and bows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bowed' looks like a verb (took a bow) but is an adjective, curved. 'moving' and 'to the front' together shift the R of the assistant's title to its start.
explanation.definitionFit: Arcuate is a technical term for curved like an arch, so it means bent or bowed in shape.

clue.text: Old king and duke wreathed sinuously in tree

indicators.note: the duke and the rearranged letters are placed inside the name of the tree

parts.note: the elder is a small tree with white flowers and black berries

indicators.note: sinuously means twisting and winding, so the letters of the word wreathed bend into a new order

explanation.surface: A monarch and a nobleman, twisted into garlands, sit up in a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sinuously' rearranges 'wreathed'; 'in' places the duke plus those letters inside the tree name, just after its first letter, giving the tenth-century king.
explanation.definitionFit: Edward the Elder was an Anglo-Saxon ruler of the tenth century, son of Alfred the Great.

clue.text: Work out 1055 + 19 for stimulation

indicators.note: to work something out can mean to rearrange it, so the letters are shuffled

parts.note: 1055 in Roman numerals is MLV
nineteen written out as a word

explanation.surface: A simple arithmetic sum offered as a stimulating mental exercise.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like a maths task, but 1055 becomes Roman numerals and 19 is spelt out; 'Work out' rearranges the lot.
explanation.definitionFit: Enlivenment is the act of making livelier, which is a form of stimulation or rousing.

clue.text: Perhaps use a rotary trimmer, hardly changed after turning 180 degrees

definitions.meaning: to cut grass with a rotary lawn machine
the three capital letters, rotated upside down, read exactly the same

explanation.surface: Gardening advice about a lawn cutter that looks no different after a half turn.
explanation.walkthrough: Written in capitals and turned upside down, the M becomes a W, the O stays, and the W becomes an M, so the word reads the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Cutting grass with a rotary mower is what this verb names; the second part is a visual trick on the capitals.

clue.text: One welcomed by European gourmand?

indicators.note: the eater takes in the numeral one as a guest, holding it inside

parts.note: a scoffer is someone who scoffs, or eats greedily
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A guest received at the table of a greedy European eater.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as a description: the celebrated French chef was a European whose cooking food lovers welcomed.
explanation.definitionFit: Auguste Escoffier, the celebrated French chef, stands as the archetypal European master of fine eating.

clue.text: Inward changes with pale exterior over a large area

indicators.note: the word for growing pale forms the outside, with the rearranged letters within it

parts.note: to fade is to grow pale

indicators.note: changes means the letters of the word inward are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: Something turning inward while showing a pale outside, spread across a wide expanse.
explanation.walkthrough: Pale is a verb here: to grow faint, fade.
explanation.definitionFit: Something spread across great distances in every direction covers an extensive region.

clue.text: Gagging period stops medical drama

indicators.note: the period plugs the gap inside the drama's title, as a stopper fills a hole

parts.note: ER was a long-running US hospital television drama
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: A TV hospital drama interrupted by a long spell of choking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gagging' is British slang for desperately keen, not choking.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang someone gagging for something is keen and impatient to have it.

clue.text: Hanky's not any good for holding watery liquids

indicators.note: the first pair of words grips the liquids inside them

parts.note: no means not any
sera, plural of serum, are watery fluids of the body

explanation.surface: A complaint that a handkerchief is no use for absorbing liquids.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's in 'Hanky's' stands for 'is', linking definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A nose rag is a slang term for a handkerchief.

clue.text: Sinn Fein members finally elect senior church official

parts.note: the Provos, the Provisional IRA, were the armed wing linked to Sinn Fein, the Irish republican party

indicators.note: finally means only the last letter of the following word is used

explanation.surface: Irish republicans voting in a senior figure of the church.
explanation.walkthrough: The page reads 'Sinn in', almost certainly 'Sinn Fein' with the letters F, E lost. 'Provos' is the nickname of the Provisional IRA.
explanation.definitionFit: A provost is the head of a cathedral chapter in some churches, a senior clerical post.

clue.text: Partial uniform?

definitions.meaning: read literally, belonging to a single part or portion of something

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means consistent or in keeping, i.e. uniform, while read literally it suggests being a fragment or portion.

clue.text: Actress Hatcher perhaps collecting silver

indicators.note: the bird gathers up the metal symbol inside itself

parts.note: a hen hatches eggs, so it is one example of a hatcher
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: Teri Hatcher, the TV actress, winning a silver award.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Actress Hatcher' looks like Teri Hatcher, but the definition is just 'Actress' (Uta Hagen) and the hatcher is a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Uta Hagen was a German-American stage performer and celebrated acting teacher.

clue.text: It pains me to support Greek complainer

indicators.note: in a down entry the second piece sits beneath the first, holding it up

parts.note: ouch is what someone says when hurt

explanation.surface: A grumbler reluctantly backing a Greek, despite the pain.
explanation.definitionFit: A grouch is a habitually grumpy person who grumbles a lot.

clue.text: To France he departed since in Hackney he is uncomfortable

parts.note: il is French for he
late means dead, departed
as can mean since or because
a Cockney drops the h, saying he as 'e; Hackney is a district of East London

explanation.surface: A man left for France because he felt ill at ease living in East London.
explanation.walkthrough: Hackney is in London's East End, home of Cockney speech, which drops initial H.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling ill at ease is an idiom for being awkward or uneasy.

clue.text: Repeated series from monotonous artist

indicators.note: a run of letters that occurs twice in a row within the word is lifted out of it

explanation.surface: A dull, repetitive set of works from a tedious painter.
explanation.walkthrough: The three-letter run appears twice inside 'monotonous', hence 'Repeated'.
explanation.definitionFit: Yoko Ono is a Japanese conceptual artist and musician.

clue.text: Retreat backing onto earnest, sensitive rock monument to fighters

indicators.note: the turned piece is fixed on to the end of the others

parts.note: warm can mean heartfelt, earnest
emo is a confessional, emotional style of rock music

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the word for a retreat is read in reverse

parts.note: a lair is a hiding place or retreat

explanation.surface: A hideaway set against a solemn rock face, standing as a memorial to soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: A war memorial is a monument honouring those who fought and died in conflict.

clue.text: Fine sweet wine uncapped

indicators.note: with its cap removed, so the wine's name loses its first letter

parts.note: Tokay is a sweet Hungarian dessert wine

explanation.surface: Praise for a sweet wine served with its cork drawn.
explanation.definitionFit: Okay means all right or acceptable, as fine does.

clue.text: I'll get message disguised, made over, including chapter in reverse

indicators.note: the whole assembled word is read backwards, end to start
the word for made over takes the chapter letter inside it

parts.note: something made over has been redone

explanation.surface: A spy promising to hide a message, rewritten with a chapter put in backwards.
explanation.walkthrough: REDONE with C inside gives REDOCNE; 'in reverse' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: An encoder is a device or person converting plain text into cipher, so it renders a message secret.

clue.text: Portion of windpipe mostly containing

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Portion of windpipe mostly containing' (7): TRACHE(A) needs an N inside, but the word supplying N is missing after 'containing'; no scan or search gives it.
